title: Counting obstruction for low-degree squarefree approximation on the root cube
statement:
Let $K$ be a finite field, let $\omega \in K$ satisfy $\omega \neq 1$, and fix natural numbers $n, D, e, B$. Suppose the ball bound
\[
\sum_{t=0}^{e} \binom{2^n}{t}\,\abs{K}^{\,t} \;\le\; B
\]
holds, together with the strict counting inequality
\[
\abs{K}^{\,2^n} \;>\; \abs{\mathcal{S}_{n,D} \to K}\cdot B .
\]
Then it is \emph{not} the case that every function $f : \{1,\omega\}^n \to K$ admits a multivariate polynomial $Q \in K[X_i : i \in \mathrm{Fin}\,n]$ of total degree at most $D$ that disagrees with $f$ on at most $e$ points of the cube $\{1,\omega\}^n$; that is, some $f$ fails to be approximated in this sense by any such $Q$.
hypotheses_covered: ball bound: sum_{t=0}^{e} C(2^n, t) |K|^t <= B
n, D, e, B are natural numbers

Let $K$ be finite and $\omega \ne 1$.  Suppose the ball bound
$\sum_{t=0}^{e} \binom{2^n}{t}\,\abs{K}^{\,t} \le B$ holds and the counting is strict,
\[
\abs{K}^{2^n} \;>\; \abs{\mathcal{S}_{n,D} \to K}\cdot B .
\]
Then it is \emph{not} the case that every function $f : \{1,\omega\}^n \to K$ admits a
